explanation: Palaeontologists call the spiked tail a thagomizer, a word borrowed from a Gary Larson Far Side cartoon. The plates may have served for display, temperature control, or both.

claims.text: Stegosaurus had large bony plates along its back and spikes on its tail.
Triceratops, Diplodocus and Velociraptor did not have back plates and a spiked tail.
The spiked tail of stegosaurs is informally called a thagomizer, a term taken from a Gary Larson Far Side cartoon.
The purpose of Stegosaurus's plates is debated, with display and temperature control the main ideas.

Triceratops had horns and a frill, Diplodocus a whip-like tail and Velociraptor sickle claws; none had back plates with a spiked tail.

evidence.summaryExcerpt: Gary Larson coined the word as a joke in his single-panel comic The Far Side. In a 1982 The Far Side comic, a group of cavemen are taught by a caveman lecturer that the spikes on a stegosaur's tail were named "after the late Thag Simmons". The name was then taken up by scientists. Paleontologist Kenneth Carpenter used the term when describing a fossil at the Society of Vertebrate Paleontology Annual Meeting in 1993.
